title: Bangladesh visa centres in Kolkata and Siliguri to shut after November 30
dek: Dhaka has not renewed its contract with the company that runs them, its Kolkata mission says. Where people in Bengal will apply from 1 December has not been announced.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bangladesh's visa application centres in Kolkata and Siliguri will stop working after 30 November, the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has said, because Dhaka has decided not to renew its contract with the company that runs them. No replacement has been named, leaving travellers from West Bengal without a confirmed place to apply for a Bangladeshi visa from 1 December.

In a public notice dated 17 November, the mission said the visa outsourcing agreement between the government of Bangladesh and DU Digital Global Ltd "would expire on November 30, 2026", and advised applicants not to submit applications at the two centres after that date, according to reports of the notice. The addresses of new centres and the name of the operator that will run them will be announced in a separate notice, it said. It gave no reason for the decision.

## What changes for applicants

The two centres, in Kolkata and Siliguri, are where most people in West Bengal hand in Bangladeshi visa applications: families with relatives across the border, traders, students, patients' companions and tourists. Under outsourcing, a private company accepts the forms, fees and passports and returns them, while the mission decides on the visas.

The notice covers only the closure of the two centres. It does not say Bangladesh is stopping visa services in India, and it does not say what will happen to applications and passports already submitted that are still being processed on 30 November. Applicants have been told to wait for further instructions. People planning to travel to Bangladesh in December may have to wait until the new arrangement is announced.

The directive was issued "on the orders of the competent authorities" and sent to the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, the foreign ministry in Dhaka and DU Digital's Kolkata office, one report said.

## Background

The Kolkata centre, Bangladesh's first official visa application centre in India, opened in Salt Lake in December 2021, and the Siliguri centre followed in 2022.

Visa services between the two countries have been disrupted several times since the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government in August 2024. In December 2025 Bangladesh suspended visa and consular services at its High Commission in New Delhi, its mission in Agartala and the Siliguri centre, and in January 2026 it suspended most visa services at the Kolkata mission except business and work visas, according to reports at the time.

The change comes as relations remain strained. The fifth round of the India-Bangladesh Consular Dialogue, which was to cover visas, detained nationals and border management in Dhaka on 17 and 18 November, was postponed, and the Ministry of External Affairs said it would be held "on a mutually convenient date". Bangladesh's government under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has also sought the extradition of Ms Hasina, who has lived in India since August 2024, while her banned Awami League holds protests and "lockdowns" in Bangladesh.

## What happens next

The Deputy High Commission is expected to issue a second notice naming the new operator and addresses before 1 December. Neither DU Digital Global nor the Bangladesh mission had commented publicly beyond the notice by Saturday. India's Ministry of External Affairs has not commented.
